title: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim
wiki_lead:
The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim is a 2011 action role-playing game developed by Bethesda Game Studios and published by Bethesda Softworks. It is the fifth main installment in The Elder Scrolls series, following The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion (2006), and was released worldwide for Windows, PlayStation 3, and Xbox 360 on November 11, 2011. Skyrim was developed using the Creation Engine. The team opted for a rugged, largely sub-arctic world, after Oblivion's Imperial Province of Cyrodiil, which game director and executive producer Todd Howard considered more unique by comparison.
The game is set 201 years after the events of Oblivion and takes place in Skyrim, the northernmost province of Tamriel, a continent on the planet Nirn. Its main story focuses on the player character, the Last Dragonborn, on their quest to defeat Alduin the World-Eater, a dragon prophesied to destroy the world. Throughout the game, the player completes quests and develops the character by improving skills. The game continues the open world tradition of its predecessors by allowing the player to travel to discovered locations in the game world at any time, and to ignore or postpone the main storyline indefinitely.
Upon release, the game received critical acclaim, with praise for its character advancement, world design, visuals, and the ability to dual-wield in combat. Criticism targeted the melee combat, dragon battles, and numerous technical issues at launch. The game shipped over seven million units within the first week of its release and over 20 million by June 2013, while by July 2026 total sales reached 65 million copies. It is considered one of the greatest video games ever made, and is credited with influencing later fantasy and open-world games.
Three downloadable content (DLC) add-ons were released: Dawnguard, Hearthfire and Dragonborn, which were bundled along with the base game into the Legendary Edition released in June 2013. A remastered version subtitled Special Edition, containing all three DLC add-ons along with a graphical upgrade, was released in October 2016; a port for the Nintendo Switch was released in November 2017 alongside a separate virtual reality-only version titled Skyrim VR. In addition, the remastered version was bundled with additional Creation Club content and released as the Anniversary Edition in 2021–2022. A sequel, The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel, is in development.

Gameplay

The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim is a fantasy action role-playing game, playable from a first- or third-person perspective. The player may freely roam over the land of Skyrim, an open world environment based on Scandinavia consisting of wilderness expanses, dungeons, caves, cities, towns, fortresses, and villages. Players may navigate the game world more quickly by riding horses, paying for a ride from a city's stable, or utilizing a fast-travel system that allows them to move their character immediately to a previously discovered location.

grok_lead: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim is an action role-playing open-world video game developed by Bethesda Game Studios and published by Bethesda Softworks. Released on November 11, 2011, for Microsoft Windows, PlayStation 3, and Xbox 360, it serves as the fifth main installment in The Elder Scrolls series, following The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion. The game is set in the fictional province of Skyrim, the northernmost region of the continent Tamriel, where players control a customizable protagonist known as the Dragonbornâa mortal with the soul of a dragonâwho emerges amid escalating threats including the return of ancient dragons and a brewing civil war. The core narrative centers on the Dragonborn's quest to confront Alduin, the prophesied World-Eater dragon foretold to destroy the world, while navigating the political turmoil of Skyrim's civil war between the Imperial Legion, loyal to the Empire of Tamriel, and the Stormcloak rebels seeking independence for the province. The outcome of the civil war is determined by the player's choices and has no official canonical resolution or winner in the broader Elder Scrolls lore; Bethesda has not declared a definitive result. Former Skyrim lead designer Bruce Nesmith has speculated that The Elder Scrolls VI may leave the outcome undefined or depict it as unresolved to preserve narrative flexibility. As of September 2026, The Elder Scrolls VI remains unreleased, with no confirmed details on its handling of Skyrim's player choices or the civil war. Players experience this story through a vast, seamless open world spanning mountains, forests, ancient ruins, and Nordic-inspired cities, with opportunities to join factions, complete side quests, and shape their character's path via skill progression in combat, magic, stealth, and crafting. Gameplay emphasizes freedom of choice, allowing first- or third-person perspectives, real-time combat with melee weapons, spells, and shouts (dragon language powers), and non-linear exploration without traditional class restrictions. Upon release, Skyrim received widespread critical acclaim for its immersive world-building, depth of content, and technical achievements in open-world design, earning over 200 Game of the Year awards from various publications and organizations. Commercially, it shipped more than 7 million units in its first week and has sold over 65 million copies worldwide as of July 2026, making it one of the best-selling video games of all time. The title has seen multiple re-releases, including the Skyrim Special Edition in 2016 with enhanced graphics for PlayStation 4, Xbox One, and PC; ports to Nintendo Switch and PlayStation VR in 2017; and the Skyrim Anniversary Edition in 2021, incorporating all official expansionsâ Dawnguard, Hearthfire, and Dragonborn âalong with over 70 Creation Club add-ons for additional quests, items, and environments; and a port of the Anniversary Edition to the Nintendo Switch 2 in December 2025 with enhanced visuals. As of September 2026, The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim Special Edition is available on Xbox Game Pass, included with Premium and Ultimate subscriptions with cloud streaming support, while the Anniversary Edition is discounted for Game Pass members but not fully included. Its enduring popularity has spawned a dedicated modding community, influencing subsequent Bethesda titles and solidifying its status as a landmark in role-playing games.
